content.title: About
content.content: Whole wheat bread is made from whole grain wheat that includes the bran, germ, and endosperm. It has a dense crumb, a slightly nutty aroma, and a darker color compared to white bread. This bread is commonly used for sandwiches, toast, and as a side to soups.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole wheat bread contains all parts of the grain, making it more nutritious than refined flour bread.
It became popular in Europe during the Middle Ages when whole grains started to be milled for baking.
The high fiber content helps regulate blood sugar levels.
In many countries, whole wheat bread is a staple and is included in national dietary guidelines.
The dark color comes from melanoidins formed during baking of whole grains.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Fiber improves digestion, promotes satiety, and helps maintain healthy cholesterol levels.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Whole wheat bread provides thiamine, niacin, and folate, which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: It supplies magnesium, iron, and zinc, essential for muscle function and immunity.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Compared with white bread, it raises blood sugar more slowly, beneficial for weight management and diabetes control.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phytonutrients such as phenolic acids help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: People with wheat allergy or celiac disease may experience severe reactions to whole wheat bread.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: The bread contains gluten and is unsuitable for gluten‑free diets.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce the absorption of certain minerals when consumed in large amounts.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Although more nutritious, whole wheat bread still provides calories, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy it fresh or toasted, as a base for sandwiches with avocado, cheese, or vegetables. It’s also used for croutons, breadcrumb coating for patties, and as a layer in casseroles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bread in a paper bag or cloth sack at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze it in an airtight bag – it will stay fresh for up to 2 months. Thaw at room temperature before use.

frozen-mocha-coffee-drink-with-non-dairy.title: Frozen mocha coffee drink with non-dairy milk

content.title: About
content.content: Frozen mocha coffee drink is a refreshing frozen beverage made from cold coffee, chocolate syrup and non‑dairy milk (soy, almond or oat). It combines the rich flavor of coffee, a sweet mocha note and a creamy texture without any animal‑derived ingredients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The drink is a staple of summer menus in cafés and food courts worldwide.
Non‑dairy milk makes it suitable for vegans and people with lactose intolerance.
Freezing coffee preserves most of the antioxidants found in fresh brew.
Chocolate syrup is often prepared from natural cocoa, giving a deeper flavor.
A pinch of sea salt is sometimes added to enhance the taste.

items.title: Caffeine boost
items.content: Caffeine improves alertness and can temporarily enhance physical performance.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Coffee and cocoa are rich in polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Lactose‑free
items.content: Using plant‑based milk eliminates lactose, benefiting those with intolerance.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Coffee provides vitamins B2, B3 and B5, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Calcium from fortified plant milk
items.content: Fortified non‑dairy milks can supply calcium and vitamin D.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: High caffeine intake may cause anxiety, insomnia and rapid heartbeat.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Chocolate syrup adds sugar; people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Allergy to plant ingredients
items.content: Some plant milks (soy, nut‑based) can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Frozen drinks can be calorie‑rich due to sugar and cream, so consume in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the frozen mocha coffee drink in a glass with a straw, enjoying it right after thawing. Optionally top with whipped plant‑based cream, a dusting of cocoa powder, or grated chocolate.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen beverage at –18 °C in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks. Once thawed, consume within 24 hours.

content.title: About
content.content: Lactose‑free reduced‑fat milk (2%) is pasteurized cow’s milk that has had most of its lactose removed and the fat content lowered to 2 %. It retains the majority of the nutrients found in regular milk while being easier to digest for those with lactose intolerance and suitable for low‑fat diets.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lactose is removed using lactase enzymes or filtration, making the product safe for most people with lactose intolerance.
Reduced‑fat milk is popular in diet and sports nutrition because of its lower calorie content.
At 2 % fat, the milk still provides fat‑soluble vitamins A, D, E, and K, though in smaller amounts than whole milk.
In some countries, lactose‑free milk is classified as a separate food category with specific labeling regulations.
The lactose‑removal process preserves the natural taste of milk, unlike many plant‑based alternatives.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Milk is rich in calcium and vitamin D, which are essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: High‑quality protein source
items.content: A serving provides about 7 g of complete milk protein, important for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Easy to digest for lactose‑intolerant individuals
items.content: Removing lactose allows those with intolerance to enjoy milk’s nutrients without discomfort.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The 2 % fat content makes the product less caloric, helping with weight management while retaining nutritional value.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Riboflavin (B2) and cobalamin (B12) support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or whey may react to this milk regardless of lactose content.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although lactose is removed, some brands add sweeteners; check the label if you monitor sugar intake.

items.title: Possible additives
items.content: Certain products are fortified with extra vitamins or minerals; those with sensitivities should read the ingredient list.

items.title: Storage safety
items.content: After opening, keep the milk refrigerated and consume within 5–7 days to prevent microbial spoilage.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Lactose‑free reduced‑fat milk can be enjoyed plain, added to cereals, smoothies, coffee, baked goods, and sauces. It pairs well with fruit, berries, and grains and serves as a base for low‑fat desserts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the milk in the refrigerator at 1–4 °C. Keep the container tightly sealed after opening. Discard if it develops a sour smell, off‑taste, or changes in texture.

content.title: About
content.content: Mock chicken legs are a plant‑based chicken substitute made from soy protein, wheat gluten and natural flavorings that mimic the taste and texture of real chicken drumsticks. The product is suitable for vegetarians and anyone looking to reduce meat consumption while keeping familiar flavors.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mock chicken legs are often used in vegan versions of classic dishes such as BBQ wings or chicken nuggets.
The fibrous texture is created by high‑pressure extrusion of protein, producing meat‑like strands.
Flavor is enhanced with plant‑based chicken broth extracts and a blend of spices.
The product can be fortified with B‑vitamins and iron to offset nutrients lost when eliminating meat.
Many fast‑food chains offer mock chicken legs as a more sustainable menu option.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: A serving provides about 15–20 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with real chicken legs, it contains minimal saturated fat, which is heart‑friendly.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Fortified iron helps maintain normal hemoglobin levels, especially in vegetarian diets.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Wheat gluten adds a modest amount of fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Cholesterol‑free
items.content: The product contains no cholesterol, making it safe for those monitoring lipid levels.

items.title: Soy and gluten allergy
items.content: The product contains soy protein and wheat gluten, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salt is often added for flavor; people watching sodium intake should monitor portion size.

items.title: Processed ingredients
items.content: As with most meat analogues, it undergoes extensive processing, which may not suit those preferring whole foods.

items.title: Not gluten‑free
items.content: Because wheat gluten is a key ingredient, it is unsuitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mock chicken legs can be fried, baked, grilled, or roasted. They are often marinated in soy sauce, spices and oil, then coated in breadcrumbs for a crispy crust. Serve with BBQ, honey‑mustard, or spicy sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the product in a sealed container in the refrigerator at 0 °C–4 °C. Once opened, it lasts 5–7 days. For longer storage, freeze up to 3 months, packing tightly to minimize air.

pasta-with-tomato-based-sauce-and-meat-r.title: Pasta with tomato-based sauce and meat, ready-to-heat

content.title: About
content.content: Pasta with tomato-based sauce and meat is a ready‑to‑heat meal that can be quickly warmed in a microwave or on the stove. It contains pasta, a tomato sauce, pieces of selected meat and spices. Designed for convenient and tasty nutrition at any time.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The tomato sauce is made from ripe tomatoes, giving the dish a bright flavor and aroma.
The meat is usually beef or pork, pre‑seared and seasoned with herbs.
The pasta is often fortified with B‑vitamins and iron, making it nutritionally rich.
The dish can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 5 days or frozen for up to 3 months.
Heating typically takes 2–3 minutes in a microwave.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Meat and pasta provide complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in complex carbohydrates
items.content: Pasta supplies sustained energy through complex carbs, helping maintain blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Tomato sauce offers vitamin C, lycopene and potassium, while the meat contributes iron and zinc.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Thermally processed ingredients make the meal soft and easy on the stomach.

items.title: Convenient and time‑saving
items.content: A ready‑made dish provides a complete meal quickly without cooking.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The tomato sauce can be salty; people monitoring sodium intake should consider portion size.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Wheat pasta contains gluten, making the product unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Meat pieces may contain saturated fats; moderation is recommended.

items.title: Thermal safety
items.content: Insufficient heating may leave cold spots where bacteria could survive.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the meal in a microwave (800 W) for 2–3 minutes, stirring halfway through. If needed, finish heating on the stovetop while stirring. Serve hot, optionally topped with grated cheese or fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 0–4 °C for no more than 5 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C for up to 3 months. Ensure the packaging is intact before reheating.

content.title: About
content.content: Peas and carrots are fresh vegetables cooked by steaming without added fat. Peas have a sweet, tender flavor and a crisp texture, while carrots offer a sweet, slightly earthy taste with a soft yet firm bite.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peas belong to the legume family and are a good source of plant protein.
Carrots are one of the richest sources of beta‑carotene, a vitamin A precursor.
The combination is common in traditional dishes worldwide, from Russian salads to Indian curries.
Steaming preserves more vitamins and minerals compared with boiling in water.
Together they provide a broad range of amino acids, enhancing protein bioavailability.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Peas contain vitamin B6 and folate, supporting metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: High in beta‑carotene
items.content: Carrots deliver a high amount of provitamin A, essential for vision and immunity.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Fiber from peas and carrots promotes regular bowel movements and satiety.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Prepared without added fat, the dish fits low‑calorie dietary plans.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Phytonutrients such as lutein and zeaxanthin in carrots help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to peas.

items.title: Sugar content for children
items.content: Carrots contain natural sugars; small portions are fine for kids, but total sugar intake should be considered.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Legumes, including peas, can cause flatulence in sensitive people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve as a side dish, add to salads, soups, or use as a filling for wraps. You may season with fresh herbs, lemon juice, or a light soy sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked product in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze portions and re‑steam before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Raspberries are delicate, tender, red fruits of plants in the genus Rubus, with a sweet, slightly tart flavor. They are hollow in the center because the fruit separates from its core when picked. Raspberries also come in black, purple, and golden varieties and are eaten fresh and used in desserts, jams, sauces, and smoothies.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Botanically, a raspberry is an aggregate fruit made of many small drupelets.
Raspberries are hollow because the core stays on the plant when the fruit is picked.
Raspberries come in red, black, purple, and golden varieties.
Raspberries are among the highest-fiber fruits per serving.
They are related to blackberries and roses.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Raspberries are a rich source of fiber, which supports digestion and fullness.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and skin.

items.title: Provides manganese
items.content: Manganese supports normal metabolism and bone health.

items.title: Contains polyphenols
items.content: Raspberries contain anthocyanins and ellagic acid, which have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Low in sugar
items.content: Raspberries are lower in sugar than many other fruits.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some people may be allergic to raspberries or sensitive to the natural salicylates they contain.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large amounts of fiber and seeds may cause bloating in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Fragility and mold
items.content: Raspberries spoil quickly and can mold, so discard any moldy berries.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Conventionally grown berries may carry residues, so wash them gently before eating.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raspberries can be eaten fresh, added to yogurt, oatmeal, cereal, salads, and smoothies, or baked into muffins, tarts, and cakes. They can be cooked into jams, sauces, and coulis. Wash them gently just before eating.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Raspberries are very delicate. Refrigerate them unwashed in a single layer in a breathable container and eat them within one to three days. Discard any moldy berries right away. Freeze them on a tray and then store them in a bag for longer storage.

content.title: About
content.content: Whopper with cheese is Burger King’s signature burger made with a flame‑grilled beef patty, melted cheese, fresh vegetables, sauce and a sesame‑seed bun. The grilling gives it a distinctive smoky flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The original Whopper was introduced in 1957 in the United States.
The cheese version appeared in the early 2000s to meet growing demand for cheesier burgers.
It is sold in more than 100 countries worldwide.
Ingredients may vary slightly to meet regional regulations.
Burger King uses 100 % beef with no fillers.

items.title: Protein
items.content: The beef patty provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Red meat is a good source of heme iron, which is readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The burger contains B12, B6 and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Melted cheese adds calcium, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: Fiber from vegetables
items.content: Lettuce, tomato and onion contribute a modest amount of dietary fiber.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: A Whopper with cheese contains roughly 700–800 kcal, which can contribute to weight gain if eaten frequently.

items.title: Saturated fat and sodium
items.content: The burger is relatively high in saturated fats and salt, which may affect cardiovascular health.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Contains milk, gluten, and soy (in the sauce), which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Preservatives and additives
items.content: Some components may include food additives that are unsuitable for people with sensitivities.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The burger is served in its classic bun and is meant to be eaten by hand. You can add extra sauce, remove the bun, or swap it for a whole‑grain version for a healthier twist.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a prepared burger in the refrigerator for no more than 24 hours. For longer storage, reheat in an oven or microwave to restore the bun’s texture.
